description:
Reports when a domain registration expires, who the registrar is, and how the domain is
configured in DNS — nameservers, address records, mail exchangers, TXT and CAA records,
whether the delegation is signed with DNSSEC and still validates, and what its SPF and DMARC records say
about who may send email as it.

Use it to answer "is this domain about to lapse?", "who do we renew this with?", "where
does this domain point?" or "why does the apex not work when www does?". It is the right
first call when a site has gone dark for no obvious reason.

Use it too for "why is this client's email going to spam?" or "can someone spoof this
domain?" — SPF and DMARC are read from the domain's own DNS.

It also asks each of the domain's own nameservers, directly, whether they agree about
the zone. That answers "why does this site work for some people and not others?" and
"is this old nameserver still in the delegation?" — a question no recursive resolver can
answer, because it replies with whatever one server told it and does not say which.
Pass checkNameservers: false to skip it.

Do not use it to check whether a website responds — that is uptime_check — or to inspect
an SSL certificate, which is ssl_check. It reads only what registries and DNS publish.
It reports no DKIM: finding a DKIM key needs its selector, and a selector cannot be
discovered without guessing at names, which this project will not do.

Registration data comes from RDAP. Some country registries (.de, .nl, .no, .au, .fi)
publish no expiry date at all; the result says so explicitly rather than reporting a gap
as if it were an unknown. An expiry inside 30 days is reported as a warning and inside
seven days as critical — a manual renewal needs that much lead time. Returns findings
ordered by how much attention they need, worst first.

checkNameservers.description: Whether to ask the domain's own nameservers whether they agree about it, which no recursive resolver can answer. Costs one DNS query over TCP to each nameserver the domain publishes, in parallel, and finds a server left in the delegation that no longer serves the zone and a zone edited on one server and never transferred to the others. Defaults to true. Set false to skip it — the rest of the check is unaffected. Example: false

domain.description: The domain to check, e.g. "example.com" — no scheme, no trailing slash. A full URL such as "https://example.com/pricing" is also accepted and reduced to its hostname. Internationalised names ("café.pt") are accepted and converted automatically. Registration is a property of the registrable domain, so "www.shop.example.co.uk" is checked as "example.co.uk". A bare public suffix such as "co.uk" is refused: nobody owns one, so there is nothing to check.

name: domain_check

checkedAt.description: When the check ran, ISO 8601 in UTC.

dns.description: DNS records for the registrable domain.

apexResolves.description: Whether the domain itself has an address record.

caa.description: CAA records. The tag is the property name, e.g. { critical: 0, issue: "..." }.

dmarcTxt.description: TXT records at "_dmarc." plus the domain, where DMARC is published.

mx.description: Mail exchangers, lowest priority first. An empty exchange is RFC 7505 "null MX".

ns.description: Nameservers, lowercased and without a trailing dot.

txt.description: TXT records, each already joined from its chunks.

unanswered.description: Record sets the resolver could not answer for while it answered the others. Each is empty above because nothing is known about it, not because the domain publishes none. Empty when every question was answered.

reason.description: Why, with the resolver's code, e.g. "the resolver returned SERVFAIL (ESERVFAIL)".

recordSet.description: The field above that could not be read; "wwwA" and "wwwAaaa" are the address records of "www." plus the domain.

wwwResolves.description: Whether "www." plus the domain has an address record.

dnsResolved.description: Whether the DNS lookup answered at all. When false every field under "dns" is empty because nothing could be read, not because the domain has no records.

dnssec.description: Whether the delegation is signed and, when it is, what a validating resolver makes of it.

delegationSigned.description: Whether the parent zone publishes a DS record. Null when it could not be established.

source.description: Where the answer about the delegation came from.

validation.description: Cloudflare's validating resolver's verdict on a signed delegation; this tool verifies no signature itself. `broken` is `dnssec_broken`: the domain is unreachable for validating resolvers and certificates cannot be renewed. Null when the delegation is not known to be signed, or the resolver gave no verdict.

domain.description: The hostname that was checked, in ASCII (punycode) form.

email.description: Email authentication, read from the domain's own TXT records. DKIM is not reported: finding a DKIM key needs its selector, which cannot be discovered without guessing.

dmarc.description: DMARC: what receivers should do when authentication does not line up.

policy.description: The "p=" tag: "none" monitors only, "quarantine" sends failures to spam, "reject" refuses them. Null when the record names no valid policy.

record.description: The record as published, or null if absent.

recordCount.description: How many "v=DMARC1" records exist. More than one is invalid.

reportingAddresses.description: The "rua=" addresses aggregate reports go to, as published.

unavailableReason.description: Why the record could not be read, or null when it was. When set, "present" is false because nothing is known, not because nothing is published.

spf.description: SPF: which servers may send mail as this domain.

all.description: What the "all" mechanism says about unlisted senders: "fail" is -all, "softfail" is ~all, "neutral" is ?all, "pass" is +all or a bare all. Null when absent.

directLookups.description: Terms in this record that cost a DNS lookup. A lower bound: it does not follow include: or redirect=, so over the limit proves a broken record and under it proves nothing.

record.description: The record as published, or null if absent.

recordCount.description: How many "v=spf1" records exist. More than one makes SPF fail entirely.

unavailableReason.description: Why the record could not be read, or null when it was. When set, "present" is false because nothing is known, not because nothing is published.

items.description: One actionable observation about the target.

code.description: Stable identifier for this kind of observation, e.g. "cert_expires_soon".

message.description: One sentence explaining the observation in plain words.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

nameservers.description: What the domain's own nameservers said when each was asked directly, over TCP port 53 with recursion off. This is the only way to see a nameserver left in the delegation after a migration, or a zone edited on one server and never transferred to the others; a recursive resolver answers with whatever one server told it and hides which.

agree.description: Whether every nameserver that answered holds the same version of the zone. True when none answered, because nothing was compared.

answers.description: One entry per nameserver asked, in the order the domain publishes them.

address.description: The address that was asked, or null when the name resolved to none.

host.description: The nameserver, as the domain publishes it.

outcome.description: What came of asking it. "authoritative" is what should happen. "lame" answered without authority for the zone, so it is in the delegation and not serving it. "unresolvable" means its own hostname does not resolve, so no resolver can reach it either. "unreachable" means it could not be asked over TCP port 53, which says nothing about UDP and is not by itself a fault.

problem.description: Why it did not answer usefully, in plain words. Null when it did.

serial.description: The zone serial this server holds. This is the version number of the zone, and it is what makes two nameservers comparable.

checked.description: Whether the nameservers were asked directly. False when the caller passed checkNameservers: false, when the domain publishes no NS records or its NS query went unanswered, or when the check could not be started at all.

serials.description: The distinct serials seen, ascending. More than one means disagreement.

unavailableReason.description: Why they were not asked, or which of them were left out when a domain publishes more than this tool will query. Null when every published nameserver was asked.

registrableDomain.description: The domain registration was checked against, e.g. "example.co.uk".

registration.description: What the registry publishes about this registration.

daysUntilExpiry.description: Whole days until expiry, negative if already expired. Floored, so something expiring in a few hours reads as 0.

expirySeverity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

ianaRegistrarId.description: IANA registrar ID, which identifies the registrar even when the name is redacted.

registrar.description: Registrar name, or null when redacted for privacy or not published.

source.description: "unavailable" when the registry publishes no usable registration data.

statuses.description: EPP statuses, lowercased, e.g. "client transfer prohibited".

unavailableReason.description: Why there is no expiry date, in plain words, e.g. "the .de registry does not publish expiry dates". Null when there is one.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

unicodeDomain.description: The Unicode form when the domain is internationalised, otherwise null.

title: Domain registration and DNS
